purpose: Enriched profiles for the Farm/lolcow corpus. Each record focuses on four things: when the person's notoriety/archive began, measurable page or archive size where available, how the rise to infamy happened, and what kind of public creator/personality they became.
count_policy: Counts are dated snapshots, not permanent totals. If no defensible count was found, the value is null rather than invented.

records.name: Chris-chan
records.rise_to_infamy: Sonichu creator whose prolific public posting and distinctive fictional universe attracted early trolling, reposting and documentation. Repeated public interactions created a self-reinforcing cycle: new material produced new reactions, which produced more documentation, which produced a larger audience waiting for the next event.
records.what_they_are: Internet personality, creator and diarist whose public identity became inseparable from the Sonichu universe and its enormous archive.

records.name: SammyClassicSonicFan
records.rise_to_infamy: Uploaded emotional Sonic-fan rants in 2013. The videos were rapidly reposted across Reddit, 4chan and Tumblr; the July 2013 'Stop Hating on Sonic' video became the central viral object. Parodies and reaction videos transformed a small gaming channel into a widely recognized early-YouTube lolcow case.
records.what_they_are: Former early-YouTube gaming/vlogging personality whose Internet fame later shifted toward withdrawal, maturation and a quieter online presence.

records.name: Boogie2988
records.rise_to_infamy: Rose to mainstream YouTube visibility through the Francis character and personal storytelling. As his audience expanded, personal disclosures, disputes and controversies generated a second audience devoted to monitoring and critiquing him. His later participation in Lolcow Live makes him unusually useful as both subject and producer.
records.what_they_are: Long-running YouTube entertainer and personality whose career moved from creator success into a highly documented reaction ecosystem.

records.name: Cyraxx
records.rise_to_infamy: Repeated confrontational online interactions became clips, forum posts and reaction material. The unusually long thread demonstrates the repetition mechanism: once an audience is assembled, every new incident is interpreted through a pre-existing character narrative.
records.what_they_are: Internet personality associated with long-running forum-centered attention and confrontation cycles.

records.name: Daniel Larson
records.rise_to_infamy: Short-form video and reposting turned an obscure online personality into a serialized Internet character. New clips, impersonations, trolling, public incidents and reactions continually fed a dedicated wiki and secondary-content ecosystem.
records.what_they_are: TikTok-era Internet personality whose public life became a heavily archived serialized spectacle.

records.name: KingCobraJFS
records.rise_to_infamy: Built a niche YouTube identity through music, livestreaming and lifestyle material. His direct broadcasting style allowed fans and critics to watch events unfold in real time, creating a persistent archive. His case is important because genuine fans and Farm attention can coexist.
records.what_they_are: Musician, YouTube personality and livestreamer with a long-running fan/critic ecosystem.

records.name: MusicBizMarty
records.rise_to_infamy: Important Farmer/Cow boundary case: material created around other personalities could itself generate attention, while the creator became a subject of the same archival ecosystem. His January 2025 death creates a useful posthumous-archive case.
records.what_they_are: Internet creator/troll and media participant whose role crossed producer and subject.

records.name: Amberlynn Reid

archive.qualifier: multiple dated snapshots; exact current total not established

records.rise_to_infamy: Lifestyle, weight-loss and relationship videos created a serialized personal narrative. Reaction channels and forum communities transformed individual uploads into recurring episodes, recap videos and counter-commentary.
records.what_they_are: Lifestyle YouTube creator whose highly personal content became raw material for a large reaction ecosystem.

records.name: Foodie Beauty
records.rise_to_infamy: Mukbang and weight-loss content developed into a continuing livestreamed personal narrative involving relationships and public conflicts. Each episode could be consumed directly or through a large secondary reaction layer.
records.what_they_are: Canadian YouTube/mukbang personality whose online identity became strongly associated with food content, livestreaming and recurring personal narratives.

records.name: Nikocado Avocado
records.rise_to_infamy: Moved from vegan/violin content into mukbang and increasingly theatrical food and relationship spectacle. The character became both producer and subject: the creator generated the spectacle while reaction audiences generated a second layer of content around it.
records.what_they_are: YouTube entertainer and mukbang creator known for a highly theatrical public persona and transformation narrative.

records.name: Onision
records.rise_to_infamy: Early YouTube sketch and vlog fame expanded into an extensive controversy/documentation ecosystem. The case is useful because the archive eventually contained not merely memes but years of primary-source videos, statements and responses.
records.what_they_are: Long-running online creator whose public persona became the center of extensive documentation and controversy.

records.name: WingsOfRedemption
records.rise_to_infamy: Gaming and livestreaming produced a steady stream of arguments, personal disclosures, audience conflicts and reaction clips. Participation in Lolcow Live later formalized the subject/farmer crossover.
records.what_they_are: Gaming creator and livestream personality whose audience relationship became central to his public identity.

records.name: DarkSydePhil
records.rise_to_infamy: Long-running gaming broadcasts became a source of clips, reaction videos and extensive secondary commentary. The case shows how creator longevity can itself create a Farm: there is always a back catalogue to revisit and reinterpret.
records.what_they_are: Professional gaming/content creator surrounded by a large secondary commentary ecosystem.

records.name: LowTierGod
records.rise_to_infamy: Competitive gaming and livestream culture supplied repeated confrontations, trash talk and highly clip-able moments. Short clips could circulate independently, repeatedly renewing interest in the personality.
records.what_they_are: Competitive gaming and streaming personality with a strongly confrontational public persona.

records.name: JustinRPG
records.rise_to_infamy: Early Internet material involving unusual self-presentation and fictional-character narratives circulated through forums and trolling communities. The case predates today's highly optimized creator/algorithm economy.
records.what_they_are: Historical Internet personality whose notoriety came primarily from unusual online self-presentation and audience reaction.

records.name: Terry A. Davis

archive.snapshot: not meaningful as one page count

records.rise_to_infamy: TempleOS gave him a lasting technical legacy. His unusual public communications and online appearances then became heavily archived, creating a cultural mythology around both the software and its creator.
records.what_they_are: Programmer and sole creator of TempleOS; a major Internet-culture archive subject as well as a technically significant open-source figure.

records.name: CopperCab
records.rise_to_infamy: Early YouTube viral videos circulated through reposts, forums, parody and reaction before modern recommendation algorithms dominated discovery. Useful as a baseline for the older viral-to-Farm transition.
records.what_they_are: Early viral-video personality and historical Internet meme figure.

records.name: The Amazing Atheist
records.rise_to_infamy: Personality-driven atheist and political commentary grew during early YouTube. The case demonstrates that ideological commentary can generate a Farm-like attention ecology even when the subject is not a canonical lolcow.
records.what_they_are: Long-running political and atheist commentator whose personality became inseparable from his media output.

records.name: Ethan Ralph
records.rise_to_infamy: A particularly clear Farmer/Cow inversion: a person involved in producing political/drama spectacle can eventually become one of the spectacle's principal subjects.
records.what_they_are: Political/drama-media personality whose own controversies became part of the ecosystem he participated in.

records.name: SammyClassicSonicFan
records.rise_to_infamy: Teenage Sonic rants became viral reposts across Reddit, 4chan and Tumblr. The July 2013 breakthrough generated parodies and commentary, turning a small personal channel into a recognizable early-YouTube spectacle. Later withdrawal makes the case valuable as an example of leaving the Farm.
records.what_they_are: Former early-YouTube gaming personality whose viral notoriety later gave way to a quieter online presence.

records.name: Connor Murphy
records.rise_to_infamy: A fitness creator with a large existing audience became increasingly known for dramatic changes in content and public persona. Viral reaction cycles transformed fitness-influencer fame into broader Internet spectacle.
records.what_they_are: Fitness and YouTube personality whose changing public persona generated extensive reaction content.

interpretive_model.important_distinction: A large archive measures attention and documentation, not guilt, truth, harm or personal worth.

source_notes: Know Your Meme's lolcow history is useful for terminology and historical classification.
CWCki and Daniel Larson Wiki provide unusually clear live archive counts.
Forum page counts are always snapshots and should be stored with their date/source.
Where a page count could not be independently verified, the dataset deliberately leaves it null rather than manufacturing precision.
